title: Numbers Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 28.

questions.question: Who did the LORD speak unto in Numbers 28?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:1 states that the LORD spake unto Moses.

questions.question: What must the children of Israel observe to offer unto the LORD in their due season?
questions.correctAnswer: My offering and my bread
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:2 commands the children of Israel to offer 'My offering, and my bread for my sacrifices made by fire' in their due season.

questions.question: How many lambs of the first year without spot are to be offered day by day as a continual burnt offering?
questions.correctAnswer: Two lambs
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:3 specifies two lambs of the first year without spot are to be offered day by day.

questions.question: When are the two lambs to be offered daily?
options: One in the morning and the other at even
One at noon and the other at night
questions.correctAnswer: One in the morning and the other at even
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:4 states one lamb is offered in the morning and the other lamb at even.

questions.question: What quantity of flour is required for the meat offering accompanying the burnt lamb?
options: A tenth part of an ephah
questions.correctAnswer: A tenth part of an ephah
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:5 mentions a tenth part of an ephah of flour for the meat offering.

questions.question: What is mingled with the flour for the meat offering?
options: The fourth part of an hin of beaten oil
questions.correctAnswer: The fourth part of an hin of beaten oil
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:5 states the flour is mingled with the fourth part of an hin of beaten oil.

questions.question: Where was the continual burnt offering ordained?
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:6 says the continual burnt offering was ordained in Mount Sinai.

questions.question: What quantity of strong wine is poured as a drink offering for one lamb?
options: The fourth part of an hin
A third part of an hin
questions.correctAnswer: The fourth part of an hin
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:7 specifies the drink offering is the fourth part of an hin of strong wine.

questions.question: True or False: The second lamb is offered at even with the same meat and drink offerings as the morning lamb.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:8 confirms the other lamb is offered at even with the same meat and drink offerings.

questions.question: On the sabbath day, how many lambs without spot are to be offered?
questions.correctAnswer: Two lambs
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:9 states two lambs of the first year without spot are to be offered on the sabbath day.

questions.question: True or False: The sabbath burnt offering is in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:10 states the sabbath burnt offering is beside the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

questions.question: What offerings are commanded at the beginnings of your months?
options: Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs without spot
questions.correctAnswer: Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs without spot
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:11 commands offering two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without spot at the beginnings of the months.

questions.question: Which comes first in Numbers 28: the continual burnt offering or the sabbath burnt offering?
options: They were commanded at the same time
Neither is mentioned before the other
questions.correctAnswer: The continual burnt offering
questions.explanation: The continual burnt offering is introduced in Numbers 28:3-6, while the sabbath burnt offering is introduced later in Numbers 28:9-10.

questions.question: True or False: The meat offering for the bullock at the beginning of the months is three tenth deals of flour mingled with oil.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:12 states that for one bullock the meat offering is three tenth deals of flour mingled with oil.

questions.question: True or False: The continual burnt offering includes a sin offering of one kid of the goats.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:15 states the kid of the goats for a sin offering is offered beside the continual burnt offering, not as part of it.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Numbers 28:12, what measure of flour is to be offered for a meat offering for one bullock?
questions.correctAnswer: Three tenth deals
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:12 specifies that three tenth deals of flour, mingled with oil, shall be offered for a meat offering for one bullock. This is distinct from the two tenth deals for a ram mentioned in the same verse.

questions.question: What quantity of wine is prescribed as a drink offering for a ram in Numbers 28:14?
questions.correctAnswer: One third of an hin
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:14 states that the drink offering for a ram shall be the third part of an hin of wine, differentiating it from the half hin for a bullock and a fourth part for a lamb.

questions.question: In Numbers 28:15, what animal is offered as a sin offering besides the continual burnt offering?
questions.correctAnswer: One kid of the goats
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that one kid of the goats is to be offered for a sin offering in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

questions.question: What event is celebrated on the fourteenth day of the first month according to Numbers 28:16?
questions.correctAnswer: The Passover of the LORD
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:16 explicitly identifies the fourteenth day of the first month as the day of the Passover of the LORD.

questions.question: How many lambs without blemish are offered on the first day of the feast as detailed in Numbers 28:19?
options: Seven lambs of the first year
Two lambs of the first year
One lamb of the first year
Twelve lambs of the first year
questions.correctAnswer: Seven lambs of the first year
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:19 commands offering seven lambs of the first year, all without blemish, on the first day of the feast.

questions.question: According to Numbers 28:20, what is the amount of flour mingled with oil for the meat offering for one ram?
questions.correctAnswer: Two tenth deals
questions.explanation: This verse specifies that two tenth deals of flour mingled with oil is the appropriate meat offering for one ram, contrasting with three for a bullock.

questions.question: What does Numbers 28:21 instruct regarding the meat offering for each of the seven lambs?
options: A several tenth deal for each lamb
Two tenth deals for each lamb
One third hin for each lamb
Half an hin for each lamb
questions.correctAnswer: A several tenth deal for each lamb
questions.explanation: The verse directs that a several tenth deal of flour mingled with oil be offered for every lamb among the seven lambs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the goat offered as described in Numbers 28:22?
options: To make an atonement for you
To serve as a burnt offering
To be eaten by the priests
To be a continual burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: To make an atonement for you
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:22 clarifies that the goat is offered specifically as a sin offering to make atonement for the people.

questions.question: How does Numbers 28:12–14 illustrate the importance of precise obedience in offerings?
options: It details exact measures and animals to be offered, showing obedience in specifics pleases God
It suggests flexibility in the types of offerings allowed
It emphasizes only the intent behind the offering, not the details
It allows for substitutions of animals based on availability
questions.correctAnswer: It details exact measures and animals to be offered, showing obedience in specifics pleases God
questions.explanation: Verses 12 through 14 specify exact quantities of flour, oil, wine, and animals for offerings, highlighting that faithful obedience includes following God's precise instructions.

questions.question: If the Israelites follow the instructions in Numbers 28:19–22 during the feast, what does Numbers 28:23 promise about their continual burnt offering?
options: They shall offer these beside the continual burnt offering in the morning
The continual burnt offering will be replaced by the feast offerings
The continual burnt offering will be doubled
They should cease the continual burnt offering during the feast
questions.correctAnswer: They shall offer these beside the continual burnt offering in the morning
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:23 makes clear that the special feast offerings are to be offered alongside the continual burnt offering, emphasizing continuous devotion and obedience.

questions.question: What does Numbers 28:18 teach about work on the first day of the feast?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 18 instructs that the first day shall be a holy convocation and that no servile work shall be done, indicating rest and worship.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 28:26–31, how does the offering of firstfruits relate to the concept of holiness and rest?
options: It involves a holy convocation with no servile work and specific offerings
It encourages work on that day to prepare the offerings
It replaces the continual burnt offering for that day
It requires only a single lamb without other offerings
questions.correctAnswer: It involves a holy convocation with no servile work and specific offerings
questions.explanation: These verses specify that the day of firstfruits involves a holy convocation, rest from servile work, and detailed burnt offerings, emphasizing reverence and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 28:10, the burnt offering on the sabbath is in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explicitly states the burnt offering on every sabbath is to be offered beside the continual burnt offering and its drink offering, indicating addition rather than substitution.

questions.question: In the context of Numbers 28, how might the detailed instructions about offerings teach us about the biblical virtue of integrity?
options: By showing that faithful and exact obedience in worship honors God
By suggesting that only the heart matters, not the details
By allowing flexibility in the offerings depending on circumstances
By emphasizing quantity over quality in sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that faithful and exact obedience in worship honors God
questions.explanation: The chapter’s precise instructions reflect the call for integrity in worship—not merely outward acts but faithful adherence to God's commands, as seen throughout verses 12-31.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 28:25 commands that on the seventh day of the feast, the Israelites shall perform servile work.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 25 clearly instructs that on the seventh day, there shall be a holy convocation and no servile work shall be done, emphasizing rest and sanctity.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 28.

questions.question: According to Numbers 28:23, when are the additional offerings to be made in relation to the continual burnt offering?
options: Beside the burnt offering in the morning
At night after the burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: Beside the burnt offering in the morning
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:23 specifies that these offerings shall be made beside the burnt offering in the morning, which is the continual burnt offering, indicating they are in addition to and alongside it.

questions.question: What is the nature of the sacrifice offered daily throughout the seven days according to Numbers 28:24?
options: The meat of the sacrifice made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The meat of the sacrifice made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:24 describes the daily offering as the meat of the sacrifice made by fire, which is a sweet savour unto the LORD, offered beside the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

questions.question: What activity is prohibited on the seventh day during the holy convocation as stated in Numbers 28:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Servile work
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:25 commands that on the seventh day, during the holy convocation, no servile work shall be done, indicating a day of rest and sacred assembly.

questions.question: In Numbers 28:26, when the Israelites bring the new meat offering at the day of the firstfruits, what is required?
options: A holy convocation with no servile work
questions.correctAnswer: A holy convocation with no servile work
questions.explanation: According to Numbers 28:26, on the day of the firstfruits when a new meat offering is presented, the Israelites must have a holy convocation and refrain from servile work.

questions.question: What animals are included in the burnt offering on the day of the firstfruits as stated in Numbers 28:27?
options: One young bullock, one ram, and three lambs
Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs
questions.correctAnswer: Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:27 clearly states the burnt offering includes two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish.

questions.question: According to Numbers 28:28, how much flour mingled with oil is offered for each bullock and ram respectively?
options: Three tenth deals for a bullock and two tenth deals for a ram
Two tenth deals for a bullock and three tenth deals for a ram
Four tenth deals for a bullock and three tenth deals for a ram
questions.correctAnswer: Three tenth deals for a bullock and two tenth deals for a ram
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:28 specifies that the meat offering of flour mingled with oil is three tenth deals for the bullock and two tenth deals for the ram.

questions.question: What is the purpose of offering one kid of the goats during these sacrifices according to Numbers 28:30?
options: To make an atonement for you
questions.correctAnswer: To make an atonement for you
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:30 states that one kid of the goats is offered to make an atonement for the people, indicating its role as a sin offering.

questions.question: What does the term 'continual burnt offering' in Numbers 28:31 signify in relation to the other offerings?
options: An offering made only on feast days
A daily sacrifice without blemish alongside other offerings
questions.correctAnswer: A daily sacrifice without blemish alongside other offerings
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:31 mentions the continual burnt offering as a daily sacrifice without blemish that is offered alongside the other meat and drink offerings.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the instructions on the continual burnt offering in Numbers 28:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 29:38-42
questions.explanation: Exodus 29:38-42 also describes the continual burnt offering of two lambs daily, connecting directly with Numbers 28:6 which details the continual burnt offering ordained at Mount Sinai.

questions.question: In the cultural context of the ancient Near East, what does the 'sweet savour' in sacrifices like those in Numbers 28 symbolize?
options: The pleasant aroma acceptable to God
questions.correctAnswer: The pleasant aroma acceptable to God
questions.explanation: The phrase 'sweet savour' in Numbers 28 refers to the aroma of the burnt offering which was considered pleasing and acceptable to God, a concept common in ancient Near Eastern sacrificial rites.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the structure of the offerings described in Numbers 28:11-31, involving repeated groups of animals and flour measures?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The repeated pattern of animal offerings and corresponding measures of flour and oil in Numbers 28:11-31 demonstrates parallelism, a common literary device in Hebrew scripture emphasizing symmetry and order.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'atonement' in Numbers 28:30, and what does this imply about the sin offering?
questions.correctAnswer: Kapporeth - covering or purification
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Kapporeth' translated as 'atonement' in Numbers 28:30 means covering or purification, implying that the sin offering serves to cover the people's sins and purify them before God.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 28:19 states that the animals offered for the burnt offering during the feast are to be without blemish.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:19 explicitly states that the young bullocks, ram, and lambs offered must be without blemish, emphasizing the requirement for purity in sacrifices.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 28:10, the burnt offering of every Sabbath replaces the continual burnt offering.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:10 clarifies that the burnt offering of every Sabbath is in addition to, not a replacement of, the continual burnt offering.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of continual sacrifice as found in Numbers 28:6 and 28:23-24?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:11-14
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:11-14 discusses how Christ's single sacrifice replaces the continual sacrifices under the Law, directly connecting with the continual burnt offerings described in Numbers 28:6 and 28:23-24.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What continual offering did God command the children of Israel to present daily as a sweet savour unto Him?
options: Two lambs of the first year without spot
A kid of the goats for sin offering
questions.correctAnswer: Two lambs of the first year without spot
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:3 instructs that two lambs of the first year without spot were to be offered day by day as a continual burnt offering, which was a sweet savour unto the LORD.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by the specific instructions regarding the offering of flour mingled with oil and drink offerings in Numbers 28?
options: God’s holiness and demand for purity
God’s omniscience in knowing all things
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and demand for purity
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:5-7 details offerings of flour mingled with oil and drink offerings, emphasizing the careful, holy procedures God requires, reflecting His attribute of holiness and His demand for purity in worship.

questions.question: According to Numbers 28:11, what combination of animals was to be offered as burnt offerings at the beginnings of the months?
options: Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs
One bullock, two rams, and five lambs
questions.correctAnswer: Two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:11 prescribes burnt offerings at the monthly beginnings consisting of two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs, underscoring the structured worship God ordained.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about atonement is taught by the inclusion of a kid of the goats for sin offering in the monthly sacrifices?
options: The necessity of a substitutionary sacrifice for sin
The sufficiency of good works for forgiveness
The priest’s role as the sinner’s advocate
The symbolic cleansing of water baptism
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of a substitutionary sacrifice for sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:15 and 28:30 include a kid of the goats for a sin offering, teaching the doctrine that sin requires a substitutionary sacrifice to make atonement before God.

questions.question: How does Numbers 28:16–17 connect to the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It points to the Passover as a type of Christ’s sacrificial death and the feast of unleavened bread symbolizing purity
It introduces the Sabbath as a day of rest and creation remembrance
It establishes the priestly lineage through Aaron
It reveals the future building of the Temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It points to the Passover as a type of Christ’s sacrificial death and the feast of unleavened bread symbolizing purity
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:16–17 mention the Passover and the seven days of unleavened bread, which foreshadow Christ’s atoning sacrifice and the call to holiness, connecting to the larger narrative of redemption in the New Testament (cf. 1 Corinthians 5:7).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Numbers 28:5-6 and Numbers 28:11 convey about the nature of offerings to God?
options: Offerings must be continual and offered in their due season as an expression of covenant faithfulness
Offerings are optional and based on personal preference
Offerings should be secret and without public knowledge
Offerings are only symbolic and have no spiritual effect
questions.correctAnswer: Offerings must be continual and offered in their due season as an expression of covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:5-6 describes the continual burnt offering ordained at Sinai, and Numbers 28:11 prescribes monthly offerings, both emphasizing the necessity of regular, timely sacrifices reflecting Israel’s covenant relationship with God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that repeated animal sacrifices are meaningless ritualism without spiritual value. What does Numbers 28:23-24 actually teach about these sacrifices?
options: They are a continual sweet savour unto the LORD, indicating God’s acceptance and the need for ongoing atonement
They are purely symbolic with no real effect
They were meant only as cultural customs with no spiritual significance
They were temporary and replaced immediately by prayer
questions.correctAnswer: They are a continual sweet savour unto the LORD, indicating God’s acceptance and the need for ongoing atonement
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:23-24 explains that daily offerings made by fire are a sweet savour unto the LORD, showing divine acceptance and the continuing human need for atonement and sanctification, opposing the sceptic claim.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God’s command in Numbers 28:18 to have a holy convocation and refrain from servile work on the first day of the feast?
options: God’s sovereignty over time and worship
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over time and worship
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:18 commands a holy convocation and cessation of servile work, demonstrating God’s sovereign authority to set apart times for worship and rest.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the requirement in Numbers 28:19 that all animals offered must be 'without blemish'?
options: The doctrine of Christ’s sinless perfection as the ultimate sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of Christ’s sinless perfection as the ultimate sacrifice
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:19 requires offerings to be without blemish, typologically pointing to Christ’s sinless nature as the perfect and unblemished sacrifice (cf. 1 Peter 1:19).

questions.question: How do Numbers 28:25 and Numbers 28:26 together illustrate the principle of sanctification in the life of Israel?
options: They command holy convocations and no servile work on sacred days, reinforcing separation unto God
They allow work on holy days to maintain national productivity
They prescribe fasting as the main sanctification practice
They emphasize individual freedom over communal worship
questions.correctAnswer: They command holy convocations and no servile work on sacred days, reinforcing separation unto God
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:25-26 instruct Israel to hold holy convocations and abstain from servile work on the seventh day and the day of firstfruits, teaching sanctification through dedicated worship and rest.

questions.question: What doctrinal significance does the repeated mention of flour mingled with oil in the meat offerings imply about worship in Numbers 28?
options: Worship requires both the natural and the Spirit’s anointing to be acceptable
Worship is a matter of quantity over quality
Worship is only about external ritual
questions.correctAnswer: Worship requires both the natural and the Spirit’s anointing to be acceptable
questions.explanation: The flour represents the natural substance and the oil symbolizes the Spirit’s anointing, together indicating that true worship involves both human offering and divine blessing (Numbers 28:5, 12).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Numbers 28:22 and Numbers 28:30 make with the Old Testament sacrificial system?
options: They emphasize the ongoing necessity of sin offerings to maintain covenant relationship until Christ’s fulfillment
They introduce the permanent abolition of sacrifices
They focus on the role of the temple musicians
They highlight the Levites’ exclusive right to sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They emphasize the ongoing necessity of sin offerings to maintain covenant relationship until Christ’s fulfillment
questions.explanation: Both verses command a goat for a sin offering to make atonement, showing the continual need for substitutionary sacrifice in Israel’s covenant worship until Christ’s ultimate sacrifice (Hebrews 10:1-4).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Numbers 28:9-10 and Numbers 28:25 convey about the Sabbath and holy convocations?
options: Sabbath is both a day of specific offerings and rest from servile work, signifying holiness and dedication to God
Sabbath was only a social festival without religious significance
Sabbath required no offerings but only fasting
Sabbath was to be ignored in favor of continual work
questions.correctAnswer: Sabbath is both a day of specific offerings and rest from servile work, signifying holiness and dedication to God
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:9-10 commands burnt offerings on the Sabbath, and Numbers 28:25 commands a holy convocation with no servile work, together emphasizing Sabbath as a sacred time for worship and rest.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the regularity and precision of offerings described in Numbers 28 throughout the year?
options: The doctrine of covenant faithfulness and God’s unchanging requirements for worship
The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of predestination based on sacrifices
The doctrine that rituals are more important than heart obedience
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant faithfulness and God’s unchanging requirements for worship
questions.explanation: The chapter’s detailed instructions for daily, weekly, monthly, and festival offerings underscore the importance of covenant faithfulness and God’s constant standards for worship (Numbers 28:2, 11, 16).

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining Numbers 28:14 and Numbers 28:31 about drink offerings in worship?
options: Drink offerings symbolize the pouring out of life and joy before God, integral to sacrifices
Drink offerings were optional and had no significance
Drink offerings represented human effort to bribe God
Drink offerings replaced the need for animal sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Drink offerings symbolize the pouring out of life and joy before God, integral to sacrifices
questions.explanation: Numbers 28:14 and 28:31 detail precise portions of wine as drink offerings accompanying burnt offerings, symbolizing the believer’s joyful dedication and life poured out before God.
